title: VF-MT304-FailurePolicyQuarantine
clause: Per-binding consecutive_failures + next_attempt_at_utc, exponential backoff with full jitter capped ~15min, QUARANTINED health after N failures with EventLedger alert + slow retry, never auto-delete a workspace binding, one central error_policy path

scope.summary:
GOAL: Give the fleet reconciler a single, central failure policy so one broken workspace backs off alone, the fleet never floods logs or burns CPU on a poison VM, and NO failure path ever deletes a workspace binding. This is research P3 (errors route to one error_policy callback that owns backoff - never ad-hoc tokio::time::sleep retries inside reconcile bodies), P15 (per-item exponential backoff with full jitter; per-item so one broken object backs off alone; backoff resets on success), and P16 (poison objects are QUARANTINED with a slow retry and an operator alert - K8s has no dead-letter deletion, the max-backoff cap IS the poison handling; Oxide demands per-target stall alarms; NEVER auto-delete - these are user worktrees, not disposable jobs).

SCHEMA (one forward-only SurrealKit rollout; allocate the next free number, descriptive suffix vm_fleet_failure_policy): extend the SCHEMAFULL worktree_fleet_desired_state record (MT-301's table - failure accounting keys off the fleet row because the binding row's lifecycle is owned by worktree_vm_registry and MT-305's tombstones):
   Define required consecutive_failures int default 0, optional next_attempt_at_utc datetime, required health_state string default 'healthy', optional last_failure_reason string, and optional quarantined_at_utc datetime fields; add a typed ASSERT limiting health_state to healthy, backoff, or quarantined;
   SurrealKit defines a due-scan index over next_attempt_at_utc and health_state; rollback metadata targets only the preceding SurrealDB rollout stage. No new table: the fields live on the desired-state record claimed by MT-302, so failure accounting is guarded by the same conditional SurrealDB claim lease and fencing transaction.

CENTRAL ERROR POLICY (research P3):
   pub struct FleetErrorPolicy { pub base_backoff: Duration /* default 5s */, pub backoff_cap: Duration /* default 900s = 15min */, pub quarantine_threshold: u32 /* default 8 */, pub quarantine_retry_interval: Duration /* default 900s */ }
   pub enum FleetErrorDisposition { RetryAfter { delay: Duration }, Quarantine { alert: FleetQuarantineAlert } }
   pub fn on_reconcile_error(policy: &FleetErrorPolicy, consecutive_failures: u32, error: &FleetReconcilerError, jitter: f64 /* pre-drawn uniform [0,1) so the function stays pure */) -> FleetErrorDisposition
   Backoff formula: delay = min(base * 2^n, cap) * jitter (FULL jitter: uniform in [0, computed]); n = consecutive_failures. All error exits from MT-303's executor route through this ONE function - no reconcile body may sleep, retry inline, or compute its own delay (grep-enforced: no tokio::time::sleep in executor.rs/lifecycle.rs).
   On success: consecutive_failures resets to 0, health_state returns to 'healthy', next_attempt_at_utc clears - in the same claim transaction as the successful pass.
   On failure: increment consecutive_failures, set next_attempt_at_utc = now + delay, health_state = 'backoff', last_failure_reason = truncated typed error string - same claim transaction, generation-fenced like every fleet write (MT-303 discipline).

QUARANTINE (research P16):
   When consecutive_failures >= quarantine_threshold: health_state = 'quarantined', quarantined_at_utc = NOW(), append typed EventLedger alert FLEET_WORKSPACE_QUARANTINED { worktree_id, consecutive_failures, last_failure_reason, quarantined_at_utc } (this is the operator alert surface; MT-306 projects it), and continue a SLOW retry every quarantine_retry_interval (~15min) - quarantine is an alerting state, not a stop state (P16: retry forever, slowly, with alarms; silent max-backoff purgatory is the named anti-pattern). Clearing quarantine requires an explicit operator/agent action through a store method clear_quarantine(worktree_id) that resets counters and appends FLEET_QUARANTINE_CLEARED - the reconciler NEVER clears quarantine on its own (MT-303's planner already plans NoOp for Quarantined; this MT wires the health_state into ObservedVmState so the planner sees it).
   HARD RULE: no failure path deletes or tombstones a fleet row or a workspace binding. Deletion is exclusively MT-305's operator-intent-driven finalizer. Grep proof: no DELETE and no teardown call in the failure-policy module.

DISPATCHER INTEGRATION: MT-302's dispatcher skips rows whose next_attempt_at_utc is in the future (SurrealQL predicate on the claim SELECT), EXCEPT when the trigger source is an explicit desired-state change (a fresh live-query change event from a desired write bypasses backoff so operator intent is never delayed by a stale backoff window; a tick does not bypass). Backoff gating lives in SurrealQL, not in memory, so a daemon restart preserves backoff state (level-triggered discipline).

RESOURCE PRIVACY: all new columns live on the account/Principal-scoped fleet table (MT-301; resource_scope.rs ResourceScope 147-153) and every read/write goes through the scope-enforcing store - quarantine alerts carry worktree_id and scope attribution so MT-306 renders them only to the owning account (per the WP-1 resource_scope patterns, resource_scope.rs lines 1-42 module rationale).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: one forward-only SurrealKit rollout; new file vm_fleet/error_policy.rs; edits to vm_fleet/executor.rs (route errors through the policy), vm_fleet/reconciler.rs (due-scan predicate + desired-write bypass), vm_fleet/desired_state.rs (new columns on the record + clear_quarantine); tests.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read the landed MT-301/302/303 modules and the migration numbering state in the implementing worktree.
2. Write the forward-only SurrealKit rollout with typed SCHEMAFULL fields, ASSERT constraints, and a due-scan index; no down migration.
3. Implement FleetErrorPolicy as a pure function (jitter pre-drawn by caller) + typed disposition.
4. Route every executor error exit through the policy; update counters in the claim transaction; reset on success.
5. Implement quarantine entry (threshold, ledger alert, slow retry) and clear_quarantine (explicit, ledger event); surface health_state into ObservedVmState.
6. Add the SurrealQL due-scan predicate and the desired-write bypass to the dispatcher.
7. Tests (live SurrealDB + fake adapter; Spec-Realism Gate): repeated failure walks the exact backoff sequence within jitter bounds; success resets to healthy; failure N=threshold flips to quarantined exactly once with exactly one alert event; quarantined rows retry at the slow interval and stay quarantined on continued failure; a poison worktree does not delay a healthy worktree's dispatch (per-item isolation); desired-write bypasses backoff, tick does not; daemon restart preserves backoff windows (read from SurrealDB); no failure path deletes any row.
8. Run proof targets; record measured output. Implementer never marks COMPLETED.
acceptance_criteria: AC-304-1: A SurrealKit rollout adds consecutive_failures, next_attempt_at_utc, health_state ASSERTed to healthy|backoff|quarantined, last_failure_reason and quarantined_at_utc to the SCHEMAFULL desired-state table with a due-scan index; rollback targets only the preceding SurrealDB rollout stage.

AC-304-2: One central pure error-policy function computes min(base*2^n, cap) with FULL jitter (cap default 15min); no reconcile body contains inline sleeps or self-computed delays (grep proof: no tokio::time::sleep in executor.rs/lifecycle.rs/error_policy.rs).
AC-304-3: Failure accounting updates occur inside the same conditional SurrealDB claim/fencing transaction as the pass; success resets counters to healthy atomically.

AC-304-4: At consecutive_failures >= threshold (default 8) the row flips to 'quarantined' exactly once, appends exactly one FLEET_WORKSPACE_QUARANTINED EventLedger alert, and continues slow retries (~15min) - proven by live test.

AC-304-5: Quarantine is cleared ONLY by explicit clear_quarantine (which appends FLEET_QUARANTINE_CLEARED); the reconciler never self-clears - proven by test that a quarantined row survives 3 successful-looking slow-retry planning cycles without auto-clear unless the retry pass itself fully succeeds, in which case the success-reset rule applies and the test asserts the chosen semantic: slow-retry SUCCESS resets to healthy (success reset outranks quarantine stickiness) while anything short of full success leaves quarantine intact.
AC-304-6: Per-item isolation: a live test with one poison worktree and one healthy worktree proves the healthy one dispatches unimpeded (P15 per-item backoff, not global).
AC-304-7: No failure path deletes, tombstones, or tears down a workspace binding or fleet row (grep proof + code review: no DELETE, no teardown call in error_policy.rs).
AC-304-8: Backoff state is a durable SurrealDB record and survives daemon restart; an explicit desired-state write bypasses the backoff window, while a resync tick does not.
AC-304-9: Proof commands run with per-owner CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ../Handshake_Artifacts/; no SQLite/K8s/Docker/containerd/Nomad identifiers introduced (grep proof).
expected_tests: unit: backoff sequence 5s,10s,20s,...,cap with jitter bounds asserted statistically over pre-drawn jitter values
live-SurrealDB: failure increments counters in the claim transaction; success resets
live-SurrealDB: threshold crossing quarantines exactly once with exactly one alert event
live-SurrealDB: quarantined row slow-retries and stays quarantined on continued failure; full success resets to healthy
live-SurrealDB: poison worktree does not delay healthy worktree dispatch
live-SurrealDB: desired-write bypasses backoff window; tick respects it; restart preserves windows
unit/grep-backed: no deletion or teardown in any failure path
implementation_notes: IMPLEMENTATION GATE: gated on WP-1 IV verdicts + merge to main (expansion_provenance.implementation_gate); MT-303 must land first.
The policy function is pure (jitter pre-drawn by the caller) so MT-307 can property-test dispositions deterministically.

Quarantine semantics decision recorded here: slow-retry FULL success resets to healthy; partial progress does not. This resolves the P16 ambiguity ('require operator action to clear') in favor of self-healing on genuine recovery while keeping operator clearing for stuck cases.
Failure accounting lives on the fleet desired-state record, not worktree_vm_bindings, and the MT-302 conditional claim lease/fencing transaction serializes its updates.
last_failure_reason is a truncated display string for operators; the typed error and full context live in the EventLedger records (authority stays with the ledger).
All Rust; SurrealDB/EventLedger authority; no SQLite; no K8s/Docker/containerd/Nomad; disk-agnostic paths; no names with spaces.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Policy/schema MT; quarantine alerts and health states become operator-visible in MT-306's fleet panel. The FLEET_WORKSPACE_QUARANTINED ledger alert is the projection seam.

target_entries: Workspace fleet > Failure handling (backoff, why a workspace shows 'backoff', when it becomes 'quarantined')
Workspace fleet > Quarantine recovery (what clears it, why nothing is ever auto-deleted)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Quarantine entry/clear are ledger events here; FR quarantine events land in MT-306. Record DEFERRED-to-MT-306.

FLEET_WORKSPACE_QUARANTINED is itself the alert surface; additionally emit a diagnostic event on every quarantine entry so stall monitoring (Oxide per-target alarm heuristic) has a machine-readable feed.
No new long-lived process; the policy runs inside the MT-302 daemon whose liveness posture is recorded there.

risk_if_missed: A single poison workspace retries hot forever (log flood, CPU burn, IO stampede against CH restores) or - worse - a naive dead-letter path deletes a user's workspace binding; operators get no alert when a workspace stalls, reproducing the silent max-backoff purgatory the research basis names as the anti-pattern.

risks: RISK-1: Global instead of per-item backoff: one poison VM stalls the whole fleet's reconciliation.
RISK-2: Unjittered synchronized retries after a daemon restart produce a thundering herd of simultaneous CH restores.
RISK-3: A dead-letter-style path deletes or tears down a workspace binding after N failures, destroying user work.
RISK-4: Quarantine without an alert: workspaces rot in slow-retry purgatory and nobody notices (the named P16 anti-pattern).
RISK-5: Backoff state kept in memory evaporates on restart, so a restart bypasses every backoff window at once.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): consecutive_failures/next_attempt_at_utc are per-row columns; AC-304-6 poison-isolation live test.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): FULL jitter in the one central policy; AC-304-2 formula test with jitter bounds.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): No deletion/teardown in any failure path - grep proof AC-304-7 plus MT-305 owning the only legitimate teardown route.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Quarantine entry appends exactly one ledger alert and a diagnostic event; AC-304-4.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Backoff gating is a SurrealQL predicate on the claim SELECT; AC-304-8 restart test.
